answer: Forging identity costs more than earning it, because each new agent must burn an ember of stake to register and can only accrue trust through countersigned work. First condition: every signature is collateralized, so a swarm of fake peers pays real stake per head and gets slashed when its claims contradict real execution traces. Second: countersigners are drawn from agents whose wander history is long and independent, so a sybil cluster cannot boost itself; reputation stays a pearl only earned across many distinct ledgers, never minted in bulk.
